bullets.title: The Best Treatment for Insomnia Usually Isn’t a Pill
bullets.creator: Cyril Manning
bullets.note: ucsf.edu/jennifer.felder) ([@jenniferfelder](https://twitter.com/jenniferfelder)), [Aric Prather, PhD](https://profiles.ucsf.edu/aric.prather) ([@aricprather](https://twitter.com/aricprather)), and [Andrew Krystal, MD](https://profiles.ucsf.edu/andrew.krystal). This article covers the interplay of insomnia and depression, CBT-I, as well as two associated apps. Both apps, though seemingly clinically effective, appear quite cumbersome to access. Have you found a nondrug sleep aid that has helped cure your insomnia? If so, please let me know [@tferriss on Twitter](https://twitter.com/tferriss) with #sleep!

bullets.section: What I’m using with my dog
bullets.title: Slow-Feed Stainless Steel Bowl
bullets.note: My dear Molly pup [has a lot of superpowers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I7fflsbVEFg), but eating slowly is not one of them. Every two weeks or so, she’ll manically Hoover her food and puke it onto the floor a few minutes later. Not my favorite. This new bowl has totally fixed the problem. No one likes the scarf and barf! For some recent Molly photos that don’t involve barfing, [click here](https://www.instagram.com/p/CdLle06O_c9/) and [here](https://www.instagram.com/p/Cdd9QgUuARQ/).

bullets.title: “It seems to me that the real problem is the mind itself, and not the problem which the mind has created and tries to solve.
